extracted.intended_audience: readers of 18th-century political and social history; those interested in the historical development and critique of Freemasonry
extracted.subtask_description: A historical narrative tracing the spread, ritual changes, schisms, and moral/political consequences of Free Masonry in 18th-century France and Germany, with attention to claims of authenticity, secret societies, and social effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of Masonry — three degrees and London authority
rubrics_metrics.description: “Nothing was acknowledged for genuine unsophisticated Masonry but the three degrees; and that the mother Lodge of London alone could, by her instructions, prevent the most dangerous schisms and innovations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence to the three degrees (Apprentice, Fellow-craft, Master) and recognition/instruction from the London mother lodge are presented as the standard for ‘genuine’ Masonry and as a corrective against gratuitous innovations or schismatic degrees. Use of patents/instructions from London is recommended to resist despotism and preserve unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership evidences — Wort-Maurers vs Schrift-Maurers
rubrics_metrics.description: Operative Masons in some German towns differentiated into Wort-Maurers (whose proof was the word and signs) and Schrift-Maurers (who had written indentures). Borough-laws enjoined Masters to give employment to journeymen who had the proper words and signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimacy and entitlement to guild privileges could be proved either by traditional verbal/sign recognitions or by written indentures; in some jurisdictions written indentures were required for full privileges. The master’s giving of a word/token for each year's progress is a recorded procedural norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Rosicrucian/alchemical and occult innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rosycrucians (alchemists and pretenders to transmutation and universal medicine) were considered by other Free Masons 'bad Societies, and as gross schismatics.' Their alchymical and medical secrets, and practices like exorcism or ghost-raising, are described as corrosive novelties introduced into Lodges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introducing alchemy, magic, exorcism, or similar occult claims into Masonic lodges is portrayed as an unacceptable corruption of the Order’s purposes and as a source of schism and exploitation of credulous members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to gratuitous new degrees and foreign ritual despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: The French/Rosaic system’s new degrees and ornaments were at first admired but then resisted; many respectable Lodges 'resolutely adhered to the English system' rather than acknowledge the supremacy of the Rosaic Lodges of Berlin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unilateral imposition of new degrees, extravagant ritual innovations, or claims to supersede other Lodges without recognized authority risks division; appealing to original constitutions and the birthplace of Masonry is recommended to check such innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward claims of secret superiors and demands for unconditional submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts (e.g., Dr. Stark/Archidemides, Johnson/Leucht) show individuals claiming commissions from unknown superiors and requiring secrecy and unconditional submission before imparting 'secrets'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text counsels caution: require disclosure of the powers, provenance, and evidence of any alleged superior body before submitting; unconditional submission to unknown authorities is treated as dangerous and illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lodges as political hotbeds — misuse of fraternal space
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mason Lodges in France are described as 'the hot-beds, where the seeds were sown... of all the pernicious doctrines' that later fed revolution; many Lodges became 'converted... into corresponding political societies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using lodges as covert political societies or venues for promulgating partisan doctrines is presented as a corruption of their fraternal/moral purpose and a cause of social instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of moral instruction and active virtue for social stability
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Virtue is the cultivation of the human soul, and not the mere possession of good dispositions... Virtue supposes exertion.’ A national establishment for moral instruction and admonition is described as a principal corrector of social discontent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral education and active cultivation of virtue (not merely holding benevolent sentiments) are advanced as necessary standards for sustaining civil society and counteracting licentious or revolutionary tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schisms and secretive innovations produce contention and enmity
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated revolutions in ritual, the multiplication of schisms, and rival claims to authority are said to have made the Institution 'a source of contention, and of bitter enmity' rather than mutual complaisance and brotherly love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preservation of peace within the fraternity requires restraint on speculative innovations, transparent governance, and mechanisms (e.g., recognized constitutions/patents) to adjudicate disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary esoteric or miraculous claims require verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures like Johnson (Leucht) claiming transmutation, ancient Templar lineages, or other miraculous knowledge often proved to be cheats; extravagant promises (philosopher's stone, ghost-raising) disappointed adherents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat claims of miraculous powers, lost esoteric lineages, or extraordinary historical provenance with skepticism; require corroboration (e.g., independent verification, documentary evidence) before accepting or funding such claims.
